questions.text: In which country did the perfect and upright man Job dwell?

options.text: In the land of Canaan near the ancient city Hebron
In the land of Egypt within the fertile valley of Nile
In the land of Uz among the people of the east country
In the land of Haran by the great river Euphrates

questions.text: How many sons and daughters were born unto Job before his affliction?

options.text: Twelve sons and two daughters within his household
Ten sons and five daughters of his noble lineage
Three sons and seven godly daughters in his tents
Seven sons and three daughters born into his house

questions.text: What did Job early in the morning when the days of their feasting were gone?

options.text: He offered burnt offerings according to the number of them all
He fasted seven full days and nights in solemn quietness of soul
He paid a great ransom of silver into the treasury of priests
He circumcised all the young men and maidens of his household

questions.text: What question did Satan answer the LORD concerning the piety of Job?

options.text: Job hath worshipped strange gods of the heathen in secret places
Doth Job fear God for nought, having a hedge about all he hath?
Job hath gotten all his substance by deceit and false balances
Job will curse thee to thy face as soon as evening twilight falls

questions.text: Where were Job's sons and daughters eating when the great wind smote the house?

options.text: Upon the open pastures where the camels and sheep fed
In the house of their father Job within the city walls
In their eldest brother's house, eating and drinking wine
In the tents of their youngest sister near the fountain

questions.text: How did Job receive the bitter tidings of the loss of his children and substance?

options.text: He cursed the day of his birth and cried aloud before people
He sent his armed servants to pursue after the band of Sabeans
He fell down astonished and spoke not for seven full days
He rent his mantle, and shaved his head, and fell down on ground

questions.text: With what did Satan smite Job from the sole of his foot unto his crown?

options.text: With sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown
With total blindness and palsy throughout all his limbs
With grievous leprosy so that he was put from city gate
With a burning fever and consumption within his flesh

questions.text: What counsel did Job's wife speak unto him in his great affliction?

options.text: Call upon the elders of Uz that they may make intercession!
Dost thou still retain thine integrity? curse God, and die!
Sell the remnant of our goods and flee into land of Egypt!
Command thy young men to bear thee unto a cool cave to rest!

questions.text: What did the three friends do when they lifted up their eyes afar off and knew him not?

options.text: They fled away in terror fearing the infection of disease
They began immediately to reprove him with bitter words
They lifted up their voice and wept, and sat down in silence
They brought balms and poured soothing oil upon his sores

questions.text: Which of Job's three friends was the first to answer and speak unto Job?

options.text: Bildad the Shuhite of the wilderness
Zophar the Naamathite from the south
Elihu the youngest of the listeners
Eliphaz the Temanite began to speak

questions.text: What principle did Eliphaz maintain in his first speech concerning suffering?

options.text: Who ever perished, being innocent? or where were righteous cut off?
God afflicts mankind without any regard unto their righteousness
The upright must ever suffer more torment than the wicked men
Earthly sorrow is mere chance having no purpose of the Creator

questions.text: How did Job describe his three friends in the midst of their continuous rebukes?

options.text: As faithful counselors and enlightened prophets of God
As miserable comforters and physicians of no value
As righteous judges over the secret trespass of house
As merciful shepherds upon the mountains of the wilderness

questions.text: What glorious testimony of faith did Job proclaim in the depths of his affliction?

options.text: My glory shall not perish and my memorial endureth for ever
The wisdom of the ancients shall establish my righteousness
I know that my redeemer liveth, and that he shall stand at latter day
My sorrow shall vanish away as soon as morning light ariseth

questions.text: Unto man what did God say concerning where true wisdom and understanding is found?

options.text: In the secret veins of silver and deep places of mountains
In the rolls of learning written by the sages of Babylon
Upon the great waves of sea and the paths of the great deep
The fear of the Lord, that is wisdom; and to depart from evil is understanding

questions.text: Why had Elihu waited to speak unto Job until the three friends had finished?

options.text: Because they were elder than he, and he thought days should speak
Because he feared to be thrust out of the presence by servants
Because he had bound his soul with a solemn vow of holy silence
Because he waited for the coming of the ruler of the province

questions.text: Against whom was Elihu's wrath kindled, and for what cause?

options.text: Because they mocked his youth and despised his lineage at gate
Because Job justified himself rather than God, and friends condemned him
Because they neglected to offer burnt offerings upon the altar
Because Job had acknowledged his transgression before princes

questions.text: Out of what did the LORD answer Job when He began to speak unto him?

options.text: Out of a gentle cloud above the sanctuary
Out of a pillar of fire upon the mountain
The LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind
Out of a still small voice in the evening

questions.text: What question did the LORD put unto Job concerning the creation of the world?

options.text: Who measured out the broad foundations of cities?
Hast thou entered into the treasures of snows?
Hast thou filled the great sea with thine hands?
Where wast thou when I laid foundations of earth?

questions.text: Which two mighty beasts are described in the divine speeches to display God's power?

options.text: Behemoth and leviathan, made by the hand of God
The winged griffin and the great dragon of deep
The roaring lion and the unicorn of mountains
The great eagle of heaven and serpent in rocks

questions.text: How did Job answer the LORD when He had spoken unto him out of the whirlwind?

options.text: He justified his upright ways with words of wisdom
He abhorred himself, and repented in dust and ashes
He required a sign from heaven to confirm the sayings
He turned away in silence refusing to speak unto friends

questions.text: Why was the LORD's wrath kindled against Eliphaz and against his two friends?

options.text: Because they ministered no bread unto Job in his sores
Because they offered strange sacrifices upon hills
Ye have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as Job
Because they forbade young Elihu to utter his words

questions.text: What did God command the friends to offer that He deal not with them after their folly?

options.text: To fast thirty days in sackcloth in the desert wilderness
To give all their silver and cattle unto the poor of Uz
To build up the broken walls of Job's house at their cost
Take seven bullocks and seven rams, and go to my servant Job

questions.text: When did the LORD turn the captivity of Job and restore his estate?

options.text: When he prayed for his friends before the LORD
When he offered a thousand lambs for a sin offering
After he had fasted seven days in desolate silence
When the Chaldeans restored his camels and flocks

questions.text: How much substance did the LORD give Job in comparison with his former estate?

options.text: The selfsame number of sheep, camels, and she asses
The LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before
Tenfold of gold and fenced lands in all the coasts
The half of his former cattle, but abundance of gold

questions.text: How many children had Job born unto him after the LORD blessed his latter end?

options.text: Twelve sons and four fair daughters in his house
Ten sons and no daughters throughout all his land
He had also seven sons and three fair daughters
Five sons and five daughters in abundant honour

questions.text: What does the scripture record concerning the daughters of Job in all the land?

options.text: They played skillfully upon psalteries like the angels
They wrought fine linen and royal purple for the court
They were taken to be wives unto kings of the east
In all the land were no women found so fair as they

questions.text: How many years lived Job after his affliction and restoration by God?

options.text: An hundred and forty years, and saw his sons to fourth generation
Threescore and ten years in peace and continual prosperity
An hundred and twenty years like Moses the servant of God
Fifty years until he saw the children of his eldest son

questions.text: What name did Job call his firstborn daughter after his restoration?

options.text: He called the name of the first Kezia
He called the name of the first Jemima
He called the name of the first Keren-happuch
He called the name of the first Dinah

questions.text: What gift did every one of Job's brethren and sisters bestow upon him?

options.text: Ten thousand talents of silver and ten shields of war
A cup of carved ivory filled with spices of Arabia
Every man a piece of money, and every one an earring of gold
A vesture of purple from Tyre and a girdle of silver

questions.explanation: Every man gave him a piece of money (Heb. kesitah, an ancient uncoined weight of silver) and an earring of gold [ref:Job 42:11].

questions.text: With what words does the book of Job close concerning his death?

options.text: And Job was buried in the sepulchre of the kings
And his sons parted his great inheritance in peace
And his memorial was blessed among all the nations
So Job died, being old and full of days

questions.text: What was the substance of Job in cattle and sheep in the land of Uz?

options.text: Seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, thousand oxen
Ten thousand sheep, five thousand camels, two thousand oxen
Three thousand sheep, one thousand camels, five hundred oxen
Five thousand sheep, two thousand camels, eight hundred oxen

questions.text: Of what country was Bildad, one of the three friends that came to mourn with Job?

options.text: Eliphaz the Temanite out of Mount Seir
Bildad the Shuhite, coming to comfort him
Zophar the Naamathite out of the south
Elihu the Buzite of the kindred of Ram

questions.text: From whence came Zophar, the third of the three friends of Job?

options.text: From Teman in the mountains of south
From Shuah in the wilderness of east
From Naamah as third of his friends
From Ur of the Chaldees by the river

questions.text: Which beast is described in God's speech for its strength and fearlessness in battle?

options.text: The unicorn with his great horns of strength
The hawk stretching her wings toward the south
The young lion couching in the secret dens
The horse that paweth in valley and mocketh fear

questions.text: Which bird leaveth her eggs in the earth, because God hath deprived her of wisdom?

options.text: The ostrich, which leaveth her eggs in the earth
The eagle that maketh her nest on high crags
The stork that knoweth her appointed seasons
The dove that lodgeth in the clefts of rocks

questions.text: What did Job curse when he opened his mouth after his long silence?

options.text: The day of his birth and the night wherein he was conceived
The name of his godly parents and the memory of his fathers
His three friends who sat seven days with him upon the ground
The land of Uz and all the nations of the wilderness around

questions.text: How did Job describe the place of the dead in his bitter complaint?

options.text: As a place of everlasting torment and sorrow for all wicked men
There the wicked cease from troubling, and the weary be at rest
As a dark abyss without any hope of redemption from destruction
As a heavenly feast celebrated in the presence of holy angels

questions.text: What question did Job ask concerning the suffering man in his sorrow?

options.text: Wherefore doth God send no messengers unto the heathen kings?
Wherefore doth God bless only them that offer rich sacrifices?
Wherefore is light given to him that is in misery, and life?
Wherefore do the wicked live longer upon earth than the just?

questions.text: What voice did Eliphaz the Temanite hear in a vision of the night?

options.text: That God would break down the high walls of the great city
That a host of angels would restore all Job's lost cattle
That a consuming fire from heaven would burn up the sinners
Shall mortal man be more just than God, or pure before him?

questions.text: How did Eliphaz describe the chastening of the Almighty God?

options.text: Behold, happy is the man whom God correcteth and chastiseth
Woe unto the poor man whom the LORD casteth down in poverty
Cursed be every stroke of sorrow that falleth on righteous
God never correcteth his servants, but destroyeth hypocrites

questions.text: From how many troubles did Eliphaz say God would deliver the righteous?

options.text: In three troubles, and in the fourth sorrow shall turn away
In six troubles: yea, in seven there shall no evil touch thee
In ten troubles, and in the eleventh he shall grant riches
In twelve troubles, as the tribes of the fathers do testify

questions.text: What comfort did Eliphaz give concerning the wounding and healing hand of God?

options.text: He casteth off the sinners for ever and will not hear their cry
He leaveth the afflicted to physicians and careth not for them
For he maketh sore, and bindeth up: he woundeth, and his hands heal
He giveth health only unto such as never commit any transgression

questions.text: Unto what did Job compare his grief and calamity when he answered?

options.text: Unto the heavy lead of the refiner within the fiery furnace
Unto the iron yoke which an ox must bear upon the open field
Unto great mountain stones which fall down into the deep vale
Heavier than the sand of the sea: therefore my words do fail

questions.text: Unto what did Job compare his brethren who brought him NO comfort?

options.text: As a brook and stream of brooks that vanish when they wax warm
As ravening wolves of the desert that pursue a helpless flock
As burning fires in the forest that consume everything in drought
As withered thistles along the wayside that yield no shade at all

questions.text: Whose arrows did Job say were within him, drinking up his spirit?

options.text: The sharp arrows of fierce warriors from the land of Chaldea
The arrows of the Almighty, whose poison his spirit drank up
The arrows of venomous serpents dwelling in the wilderness
The arrows of wicked slander spoken by elders in the gate

questions.text: Unto what did Job compare the life and days of man upon earth?

options.text: Unto a joyful marriage feast with singing, dancing, and psalteries
Unto a royal triumph of mighty princes through the palace gates
Unto an appointed time of warfare and the days of an hireling
Unto a peaceful voyage of merchant ships sailing upon calm seas

questions.text: Unto what did Job compare the swift passing of his days?

options.text: Unto a swift runner upon the highway of an earthly king
Unto a flying eagle that hasteth to find meat in fields
Unto a fleeting shadow that is swallowed up by darkness
They are swifter than a weaver's shuttle, and spent away

questions.text: What question did Job ask concerning God's visitation of mortal man?

options.text: What is man, that thou shouldest magnify him and set thine heart on him?
Wherefore madest thou the stars of heaven if frail man must pass away?
When wilt thou send holy angels to rescue the afflicted from misery?
Doth it please thee when the kings of nations destroy one another?

questions.text: What question did Bildad the Shuhite ask regarding God's justice?

options.text: That God loveth the rich and casteth off the poor without any mercy
Doth God pervert judgment? or doth the Almighty pervert justice?
That no mortal man on earth can ever attain true wisdom in heart
That sorrow is pure chance and God careth not for the children of men

questions.text: Unto what did Bildad the Shuhite direct Job for sound instruction?

options.text: Unto the secret dreams of young shepherds in the mountains
Unto the ancient writings of the Chaldean stargazers in Babel
Enquire of the former age, and the search of their fathers
Unto his own private visions received in solitary wilderness

questions.text: Unto what did Bildad compare the hope of the hypocrite that forgetteth God?

options.text: Unto a flourishing cedar on the heights of Mount Lebanon
Unto a strong tower built of stone by rivers of Babylon
Unto a shield of brass that standeth firm in the battle
His hope shall be cut off, and his trust is a spider's web

questions.text: What truth did Job acknowledge concerning mortal man before God?

options.text: How should man be just with God, or answer him one of a thousand
That God ever preserveth holy priests from all sorrow and pain
That an earthly prince may contend with God before judgment
That the angels of heaven make satisfaction for mortal sins

questions.text: Which constellations did Job name as evidence of God's creating power?

options.text: The morning star, the flying eagle, and the bright shining moon
Arcturus, Orion, and Pleiades, and the chambers of the south
The scorpion, the twins, and the wandering fiery stars of heaven
The host of the skies, the evening star, and all great lights

questions.text: For whom did Job long to stand between him and God in judgment?

options.text: For an earthly monarch who might call God to account in court
For his own kinsmen who might plead his uprightness before men
Neither is there any daysman betwixt us, to lay hand upon both
For a host of heavenly warriors to deliver him from affliction

questions.text: With what imagery did Job describe how God fashioned him in the womb?

options.text: Cast as fine brass and refined as pure gold in the furnace
Woven as a tabernacle and bound together with purple thread
Ground as clean corn and baked into loaves for the sanctuary
Poured out as milk, curdled like cheese, and clothed with skin

questions.text: What did Job ask of God before he went whence he should not return?

options.text: Cease then, and let me alone, that I may take comfort a little
Restore all my former cattle and riches, that I may give to poor
Send down holy angels from heaven to rebuke my deceitful friends
Make known unto me the exact day when all this earth shall perish

questions.text: How did Job describe the land whence he should not return?

options.text: As a pleasant garden with green trees and running clear waters
A land of darkness, without any order, where light is as darkness
As a royal city having gates of pearl and streets of pure gold
As a quiet place of cleansing where righteous souls ascend up

questions.text: How did Zophar the Naamathite rebuke Job when he answered?

options.text: He washed Job's sore boils with oil and wept bitterly for him
He justified Job and joined with him in lamenting his affliction
Should not a man full of talk be answered, and his lies put down
He brought rich offerings of gold and silver to comfort his heart

questions.text: How did Zophar describe the searching out of the Almighty unto perfection?

options.text: It is revealed only unto holy prophets in midnight visions of God
It is like the tall rush that groweth along the banks of the river
It is kept hid within the ark of the covenant in the sanctuary
Higher than heaven, deeper than hell, and broader than the sea

questions.text: What promise did Zophar make to Job if he would prepare his heart?

options.text: Thou shalt lift up thy face without spot, and forget thy misery
The LORD shall anoint thee king over the princes of the east country
Thy deceased sons and daughters shall rise up alive out of graves
Thou shalt live without disease for ever and dwell in great wealth

questions.text: With what ironic word did Job answer his three companions?

options.text: He that is without sin among you, let him cast the first stone at me
No doubt but ye are the people, and wisdom shall surely die with you
Hold your peace together, for all your speeches are as empty wind
Ye have cast away the law and yet think to instruct me in judgment

questions.text: Whom did Job say to ask to learn that the hand of the LORD hath wrought this?

options.text: The wise men in the ancient cities of Egypt and Chaldea
The rich merchants who pass over the sea in mighty ships
The beasts, the fowls of the air, earth, and fishes of the sea
The priests at the altar and the chief elders within the gate

questions.text: What did Job declare concerning God's power over counsellors and rulers?

options.text: God ever submitteth his counsel unto the captains of the nations
He leadeth counsellors away spoiled, and maketh the judges fools
He rewardeth all earthly rulers with perpetual peace and security
He revealeth his secret purposes always to the kings of the world

questions.text: What bold declaration did Job make regarding his ways before God?

options.text: I will hold my tongue and wait until another speak for me before God
Though he slay me, yet will I maintain mine own ways before him
God hath forsaken me, therefore will I turn unto the princes of men
Whoso trusteth in mortal men hath founded his house upon a rock

questions.text: What two things did Job ask of God that he might not hide himself?

options.text: Restore all my former riches and drive away these deceitful men
Send down an angel to deliver me and bind Satan in iron fetters
Withdraw thine hand far from me, and let not thy dread affright me
Grant me length of days and raise all my children from the grave

questions.text: How did Job describe the fleeting life of mortal man?

options.text: As a high cedar of Lebanon that standeth against the wind
As a rock in the river that never changeth its appearance
Man born of a woman is of few days, and full of trouble
Man dwelleth in peace and passeth away like the setting sun

questions.text: What comparison did Job make between a cut tree and a dying man?

options.text: A tree perisheth for ever in the field, but mortal man abideth continually
There is hope of a tree if it be cut down, but man dieth and is wasted away
Both grow together in the king's vineyard and bring forth the same fruit
Neither tree nor mortal man can flourish on earth without rivers of water

questions.text: What question did Job ask concerning the death of mortal man?

options.text: Wherefore do men dig for treasures which they cannot keep at all?
How long shall the Almighty keep my afflicted soul in the grave?
When shall the nations be delivered from their cruel oppressors?
If a man die, shall he live again, till his change shall come?

questions.text: What charge did Eliphaz the Temanite bring against Job in his second speech?

options.text: Thou castest off fear, and restrainest prayer before God
Thou hast made secret leagues with the princes of Egypt
Thou hast kept back the hire of them that served thee
Thou hast worshipped carved images in secret by night

questions.text: How did Eliphaz describe the uncleanness of man before God?

options.text: He is less pure than the sun, yet clearer than the stars of heaven
The heavens are not clean in his sight; how much more abominable is man
He is cleansed only by costly burnt offerings and gifts at the altar
Only they are unclean who depart from the ancient statutes of fathers

questions.text: What portion did Eliphaz describe for the wicked and the oppressor?

options.text: He shall die in peace in a good old age and be honoured by all kings
He buildeth strong palaces that shall endure until the end of world
He travaileth with pain all his days; trouble and anguish make afraid
He is renowned through many sons and ruleth over foreign nations

questions.text: With what words did Job answer the speeches of his three friends?

options.text: Ye are faithful brethren who bear my heavy grief and weep with me
Your counsels are more precious than the finest gold of Ophir
I have heard many such things: miserable comforters are ye all
May God reward your kindness with double wisdom and understanding

questions.text: In whom did Job place his trust while his friends scorned him?

options.text: In the holy angels that minister before the high throne of God
In the kings of the east who should bear witness to his righteousness
In his departed children whom he believed were hovering near him
Behold, my witness is in heaven, and my record is on high

questions.text: What cry did Job utter concerning his blood and his affliction?

options.text: O earth, cover not thou my blood, and let my cry have no place
O heaven, hide all my weeping, that mine enemies may not rejoice
O sea, swallow up my lamentation and carry it away unto distant shores
O ye mountains, fall on me and hide me from the face of the Judge

questions.text: How did Job describe his life at the beginning of chapter 17?

options.text: My courage is strengthened and my youth renewed like the eagle's
My breath is corrupt, my days are extinct, the graves are ready for me
My heart triumpheth over the wickedness of all false friends in land
My strength is unfailing like mighty streams of water in mountains

questions.text: What did Job ask of God concerning a surety for his cause?

options.text: Give me gold and silver, to satisfy my creditors before the gate
Let my three companions stand as pledges before the judges of city
Put me in a surety with thee; who is he that will strike hands with me?
Let an angel of the heavenly host plead for my cause in sanctuary

questions.text: How did Job name the grave and corruption in his sorrow?

options.text: A pleasant resting place for all the mighty heroes of former ages
A dark prison house for them that rebel against the decrees of God
A distant palace which no man may behold before the judgment day
The grave is mine house; I have said to corruption, Thou art my father

questions.text: What did Bildad declare concerning the light of the wicked man?

options.text: The light of the wicked shall be put out, and the spark of his fire not shine
His light shall be doubled and burn brightly as the noonday sun over him
His candle shall be taken up by holy angels into the heavenly temple
His tabernacle shall be built of hewn stone and shine as a royal house

questions.text: Wherewith did Bildad say the path of the wicked man is beset?

options.text: With sweet ointment and fine garments brought out of the land of Babel
He is cast into a net by his feet, and a gin taketh him by the heel
With sharp briers and thorns planted round about by foreign enemies
With ornaments of fine gold that entice the bands of greedy robbers

questions.text: Unto what ruler did Bildad say the wicked shall be brought?

options.text: Unto the mighty king of Babylon with his iron chariots of war
Unto Pharaoh king of Egypt who maketh strangers serve with rigour
His confidence is rooted out, bringing him to the king of terrors
Unto a merciless ruler coming forth from the southern wilderness

questions.text: How did Job describe the estrangement of his kinsfolk and servants?

options.text: All his kinsfolk ministered unto him and bought new flocks for him
His servants fled out of the country for fear of the heavy disease
Brethren are far, servants answer not, and inward friends abhor him
They that dwelt in his house brought him daily meat out of kindness

questions.text: What desire did Job express concerning his words and testimony?

options.text: That they might be buried in the silence of the desert for ever
That they were written with ink upon parchment and laid in his house
That they might be sounded with a loud trumpet before all nations
That they were graven with an iron pen and lead in rock for ever

questions.text: What did Zophar affirm concerning the triumphing of the wicked?

options.text: The triumphing of the wicked is short, and the joy of hypocrite a moment
The riches of the oppressor shall abide unmoved for a thousand generations
God secretly blesseth the hypocrite with health and great strength in age
The joy of the sinner shall outlast even the wrathful judgment of the LORD

questions.text: Unto what did Zophar compare wickedness in the mouth of the sinner?

options.text: Unto sour vinegar that setteth teeth on edge and vexeth stomach
Sweet in his mouth, yet in his bowels it is turned into gall of asps
Unto sweet wine that deceiveth the heart and leadeth unto folly
Unto unwholesome fruit that bringeth forth sore fever and disease

questions.text: What did Zophar declare concerning the riches swallowed down by the wicked?

options.text: They multiply as locusts and fill all the storehouses in the country
They are seized by earthly kings to build up great city walls of stone
He shall vomit them up again: God shall cast them out of his belly
They shall be purified by mercy and left unto his children for ever

questions.text: What observation did Job declare unto his friends concerning the wicked?

options.text: All wicked men are cut off suddenly by thunderbolts in their early youth
The priests at the altar are always the richest men in the whole country
No mortal man can behold the fruit of his righteous labour in old age
Wherefore do the wicked live, become old, yea, are mighty in power?

questions.text: What did Job say the wicked say unto God in their pride?

options.text: Depart from us; for we desire not knowledge of thy ways. What profit to pray?
Teach us thy statutes, that we may preserve our gold from robbers in night
We will sacrifice unto thee so long as thou givest health and corn in abundance
Thou art the maker of all things, therefore grant us glory among the nations

questions.text: How did Job conclude his speech concerning the comfort of his friends?

options.text: Your words have ministered great comfort and renewed my spirit
How then comfort ye me in vain, seeing in your answers remaineth falsehood?
Let us arise and go together unto the altar to offer sweet incense
I confess that all my complaints proceeded only from unbelief of heart

questions.text: What question did Eliphaz ask at the beginning of his third speech?

options.text: Can an earthly monarch enlarge the borders of his realm without God?
Who can number the sands that lie upon the shores of the great sea?
Can a man be profitable unto God, as he that is wise unto himself?
May the priests eat of the holy offerings brought by sinners in land?

questions.text: What false accusations did Eliphaz bring against Job?

options.text: Job had bowed down unto Baal upon the high hills in the secret places
Job had hired foreign soldiers to overthrow the princes of the land
Job had not given water to weary, and sent widows away empty
Job had continually used deceitful balances and false measures of corn

questions.text: What counsel did Eliphaz give unto Job at the end of his third speech?

options.text: Flee into the desert and build a quiet dwelling far from mortal men
Buy new menservants and maidservants to establish thy house again
Offer a thousand rams upon the altar to turn away the burning wrath
Acquaint now thyself with him, and be at peace: thereby good shall come

questions.text: How did Job describe his earnest search to find God's presence?

options.text: I go forward, but he is not there; and backward, but I perceive him not
God appeareth only at noontide, while by night he resteth in heavens
He dwelleth upon the mountains of Edom and suffereth no man to come near
I sought him in the solemn songs of the temple, but found him nowhere

questions.text: What confidence did Job express concerning God's trial of him?

options.text: My sins are too grievous for the Almighty to judge me in righteousness
He knoweth the way that I take: when he hath tried me, I shall come as gold
My name shall be written upon pillars of brass among the great princes
The stars of heaven shall fall before my integrity can ever be shaken

questions.text: How did Job esteem the commandments and words of God's mouth?

options.text: As an intolerable yoke which no mortal man upon earth is able to bear
As ancient traditions of the fathers which one may put away in distress
I have not gone back from his lips; I esteemed his words more than food
As holy ordinances for the priests, but not for humble herdmen in fields

questions.text: What question did Job ask concerning the appointed times of the Almighty?

options.text: Wherefore are heathen altars on the hills not consumed by sudden fire?
